questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: A 30-year-old male presents with a well-demarcated, round, dusky-erythematous plaque on his left forearm that appeared 12 hours after taking cotrimoxazole for a urinary tract infection. He recalls having an identical-looking lesion on the exact same location of his forearm the last time he took this medication. Which of the following is a characteristic feature of this specific cutaneous drug reaction?

options.A: Occurs in completely random, different sites with each drug exposure
options.B: Recurs at the exact same site on re-exposure to the offending drug
options.C: Presents as a generalized, head-to-toe morbilliform eruption from onset
options.D: Fades rapidly within hours leaving no trace of hyperpigmentation

questions.explanation: FDE: oval/round well-demarcated erythematous plaque at SAME site on re-exposure. Residual hyperpigmentation. Common drugs: cotrimoxazole, NSAIDs, metronidazole, tetracycline.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: A 45-year-old obese male presents to the dermatology clinic noting a dark, thickened area of skin around his neck and axillae. On physical examination, the physician observes velvety, hyperpigmented plaques in these flexural folds. This clinical sign is most tightly associated with which underlying pathophysiological mechanism?

options.A: Severe thyroid hormone deficiency leading to myxedema deposition
options.B: Insulin resistance resulting in activation of insulin-like growth factor (IGF-1) receptors

questions.explanation: Acanthosis nigricans: velvety hyperpigmented thickening at neck, axillae, groins. Associated with insulin resistance (most common), DM2, obesity, PCOS. Malignant AN: associated with gastric Ca.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: A 26-year-old female presents with multiple asymptomatic, sharply demarcated, completely depigmented patches on the dorsum of both hands and around her mouth. She has a family history of autoimmune thyroiditis. What is the fundamental cellular mechanism driving her current dermatological presentation?

options.D: Enzyme defect in tyrosine-mediated melanin synthesis

questions.explanation: Vitiligo: autoimmune destruction of melanocytes → depigmented macules. Associated: autoimmune thyroid disease, DM1, Addison's. Wood's lamp: bright white fluorescence. Treatment: topical steroids, tacrolimus, NBUVB.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: A 34-year-old female presents with severe, painful, itchy purple spots on her wrists and ankles. On physical examination, the dermatologist describes the lesions as violaceous, polygonal, flat-topped papules. Close inspection of the surface of these papules reveals fine, white lacy streaks. What is this clinical sign called, and what condition does it confirm?
questions.explanation: Lichen planus is characterized by the '6 Ps': Pruritic, Purple, Polygonal, Planar, Papules, and Plaques. The characteristic lacy white lines visible on the surface of the lesions are known as Wickham's striae. Histologically, it demonstrates a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermo-epidermal junction with saw-tooth rete ridges.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: A 62-year-old male is admitted to the hospital with extensive, tense cutaneous blisters covering his trunk and thighs. The blisters are remarkably sturdy, resisting rupture when digital pressure is applied directly to the margins (negative Nikolsky sign). Skin biopsy shows subepidermal split formation, and direct immunofluorescence demonstrates a linear pattern of IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone. Which specific molecular structures are targeted by autoantibodies in this patient's disease?

options.C: Type IV collagen fibers within lamina densa
options.D: Anchoring fibrils of Type VII collagen

questions.explanation: The clinical description of tense blisters with a negative Nikolsky sign and subepidermal cleavage is diagnostic of Bullous Pemphigoid. This autoimmune blistering disease is driven by autoantibodies targeting hemidesmosomal proteins (specifically BP180/Type XVII collagen and BP230). This contrasts with Pemphigus Vulgaris, which features flaccid blisters (positive Nikolsky sign) due to intraepidermal cleavage from desmoglein targeting.
